title: After Texas' blue wave, what happens to Elon Musk and SpaceX?
gist: After Musk spent an estimated $474 million backing Republicans (nearly half in Texas) and Texas swung Democratic in the 2026 midterms, Eric Berger argues SpaceX will stay headquartered in Texas but Musk will likely push harder on orbital data centers and a Louisiana expansion. Democrats could pursue investigations, slow a SpaceX-Tesla merger and back SpaceX competitors, but NASA and the Space Force depend on SpaceX too much to cut contracts.

insights.claim: Since moving to Texas in 2020, Musk has concentrated SpaceX there, building Starbase, a Starlink terminal factory east of Austin, relocating SpaceX headquarters from Hawthorne in 2024, and announcing the Terafab chip plant in Grimes County with more than 100 million square feet of planned manufacturing space.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: SpaceX's asset base is deeply tied to Texas, so state political shifts directly affect its operating environment.

insights.so_what: Musk is now politically exposed to newly empowered opponents in his core operating state.
